findings.reason: §18 promises one owner of the rule and keeps two inline copies instead; the section must have `implementable_sections` and `plan_executable_remainder` share one definition, or state why the count-reader and the list-reader cannot, or the copies drift the moment the rule changes.
findings.text: the landing rule "only an explicit `done` reclassification removes declared work" is implemented twice: as `reckon/_schema.py:788:plan_executable_remainder`, which §18 names as the rule's author, and again inline in `roadmap.implementable_sections` (`classification == "implementable"`), which §16's coverage predicate then reads

findings.reason: the section must keep a numeric full-match (call the hoisted regex, not the derivation function) or route doccheck's validity question to a named owner that rejects non-section ids, or the consolidation silently widens what counts as a still-work section.
findings.text: §17 says doccheck's `_NUMBERED_SECTION_ID.fullmatch(sid)` "becomes a call to the hoisted derivation that accepts the same spellings", but the derivation `section_record_id` maps any string to a non-empty identity via its casefold fallback (`section_record_id("q1") == "q1"`), so the undeclared-plan fallback at `reckon/doccheck.py:1033` (`[sid for sid in heading_ids if _NUMBERED_SECTION_ID.fullmatch(sid)]`) would begin counting non-numbered heading ids such as `q1` or `decisions` as implementable work; the plan leaves the existing validity owner `reckon/_schema.py:372:is_section_identity` unconnected to this site

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design hides its new behaviour behind interfaces no larger than what they hide: `plan_fingerprint` keeps its signature and returns one digest, §17 exposes one named-record reader (`plan_headings`) over the private parser, and the section→digest map, the three recognised fingerprint forms and the coverage join stay in private helpers, so the added depth is not surfaced as many small public entry points.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §18 is titled "one reader of which sections are still work" yet keeps two live implementations of the landing rule (the rule §18 says is "the schema's to set" is inlined again in `roadmap.implementable_sections`), and §17 routes doccheck's numeric section filter onto the widening `section_record_id` derivation rather than a validity owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1477, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23 (read 2026-10-05T18:03:48Z). §17 adds two public definitions (`plan_headings` and the machinery-element predicate) and names what it merges or moves (six private grammars converged, `landed_section_ids` re-homed, no public name retired); §16 adds none and states that the family grows by two across §16–§18; §18 adds none and says so; no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family is added by any of the three.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the codebases it names and extends existing machinery rather than adding a parallel one: §17 consolidates onto `reckon/_plan_html.py:_StructuredSectionSpanParser` and `structured_section_spans`, reuses `reckon/interface_counts.py`'s AST census and its `read_trees`/`definitions` split, re-homes the existing `reckon/_store.py:landed_section_ids`, and §16 hoists the existing `reckon/crew/routing.py:section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates` rather than writing a second derivation.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one added layer that could have been thin, §16's coverage predicate, is explicitly justified: it does not forward to a single reader but joins the outstanding-section set to the union of stored section digests, and §17's `plan_headings` transforms the parser's tuples into named records rather than re-exposing them.
